question: Does the text a J++ lens is fitted on change what it reads? Lenses on Qwen3.6-27B read places and people better than numbers, and every published open lens is fitted on raw WikiText while our instruction model is read inside its chat template: are those the fitting data?
why: Chosen by the human (Zach, 2026-10-16, after a meeting with Danyil): J++ only, 25 fitting prompts per lens, domains math (OpenWebMath), chat-formatted (UltraChat) and a mix; the router refit on each domain. The second WikiText draw (wiki_b) as the noise floor was the agent's proposal in the design the human answered; the human did not remove it.

tools.wrapper: scripts/exp19_fit_data/jpp_pool_cli.py: jpp_cli.py with the router on the GPU (as neuronpedia's jpp_cli_gpu.py) and jlens.examples.load_wikitext_prompts replaced by the pool in $FIT_POOL_JSON, so the router (first 1000) and the shards (first 25) read the condition's pool

pools: scripts/exp19_fit_data/make_pools.py: 1000 texts each, the first qualifying records of each stream (>= 600 characters, cut at 2000). wiki_a is exactly the J++ recipe's WikiText pool (checked); wiki_b the next 1000 WikiText records; math open-web-math/open-web-math; chat HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k train_sft rendered with Qwen3.6-27B's chat template (enable_thinking=False; earlier assistant turns carry no think block); mix = wiki_a, math, chat interleaved (first 25: 9 WikiText, 8 math, 8 chat).

fit.recipe: J++ (neuronpedia fit-jpp-lens.sh steps): grade -> fit-router (1000 pool texts, K=8, PCA 64, skip first 16 positions, 128 tokens) -> fit-shard (first 25 pool texts, rlens LRP, 16 Jacobian rows per pass) -> merge-experts (also writes the pooled lens: the experts' rlens-LRP Jacobians averaged, i.e. an R-lens on the same data) -> fit-weights (expert weights on the eval items' fitting split fit:0, the same for every condition)
fit.layers: 0-62 (every block but the last, 63, the transport target)
fit.differs_from_recipe: 25 shard prompts instead of 64 (the human's choice); the router pool is the condition's, not always WikiText
fit.supersedes: fit_v1, whose manifest said 32 Jacobian rows per pass: 32 ran out of GPU memory in a smoke test before any fit, so fit_v1 never ran; 16 is the recipe default and changes batching, not the estimate

evals.primary: J++'s readout evals (multihop, multilingual, typo, association, poetry) by jpp_cli.py evaluate on the held-out split held-out:0 (the expert weights never saw these items): pass@1 and pass@10 per family, item-weighted, for each condition's J++ lens and pooled (R-lens) lens
evals.references: the published Qwen3.6-27B J++ (WikiText, 64 prompts) and J-lens (WikiText, 1000 prompts) from neuronpedia/jacobian-lens at the revision in pins.py, and the logit lens, in the same evaluate call
evals.planned_after: a chat-formatted read (exp08's brew protocol inside the chat template) and Anthropic's arithmetic set; not part of this run

decision.domain_changes_family: a condition changes a family if its pass@10 minus wiki_a's has a paired bootstrap 95% CI over held-out items (10,000 resamples, seed 0) excluding 0 and is larger in size than the noise floor
decision.H1_math_numbers: math above wiki_a on multihop items whose intermediate is a number (digits or a number word), not on the other multihop items
decision.H2_chat: no prediction on these raw-text evals (they are not chat formatted); reported, tested later on chat-formatted reads
decision.H3_mix: mix no worse than wiki_a on any family (no family below by the rule above)
decision.n_25_cost: wiki_a against the published J++ (64 prompts) shows what fitting on 25 prompts costs
